report.biggest_gap_example: "Was responsible for assisting with daily operational tasks." gives no process, volume, or result, so the reader cannot judge your operating contribution.
report.first_impression: The resume shows recent operations exposure across logistics, retail, campus events, and supply chain work. Most bullets describe assigned duties rather than what you changed, managed, or completed, so the target level is difficult to place.
gaps: Your operations roles do not show workload, scale, or measurable results, leaving the level of responsibility unclear.
The objective uses broad claims such as being a team player instead of naming the operations work you can perform now.
The resume does not explain which systems, processes, or reporting methods you used beyond Microsoft Office.

questions.question: How many records, reports, meetings, or schedules did you manage at Greenfield Logistics?
questions.why: The role lists recurring coordination work but gives no volume or cadence.

questions.question: At QuickMart or Greenfield Logistics, what error, deadline, or service issue did you help resolve?
questions.why: The resume does not show how you performed when accuracy or timing mattered.

questions.question: What process improvement training did you participate in, and what changed afterward?
questions.why: This may be useful operations evidence, but the current bullet stops at participation.

questions.question: Which departments did you coordinate with at Greenfield Logistics, and what did you help move forward?
questions.why: The resume names departmental coordination without identifying the parties or work involved.

questions.question: What event logistics did you organize from planning through completion at the Campus Events Office?
questions.why: The coordinator title suggests useful ownership, but the bullets do not show the full workflow.

missing: No target-role requirements were provided for comparison

next_steps: Rewrite the Greenfield Logistics bullets around the records, reports, meetings, schedules, and department coordination you handled, adding verified volume or results.
Replace the objective with a two-line operations summary naming your logistics, inventory, reporting, and scheduling experience.
Add a concise skills line using only systems and methods you actually used, including Microsoft Office and any verified inventory, reporting, or records tools.

report.score_comment_long: The resume has relevant entry-level operations exposure and a clear business degree. Nearly every experience bullet remains a general duty, with no quantified workload, process result, or named system beyond Microsoft Office. Rewrite the recent roles first, using verified scope and results.
report.score_comment_short: Relevant operations exposure is present, but the bullets rarely show scope, ownership, or results.
report.score_plain: This may qualify you for entry-level operations roles, but many applicants will appear more job-ready because their bullets show what they handled and what changed.

Education.fix: No change needed unless it improves role alignment.
Education.working: The Bachelor of Business Administration, university, and May 2023 graduation date are easy to find and relevant to the target direction.

Skills.fix: Add only if it helps the role story.

Summary.fix: Replace the objective with two lines naming your operations experience, core work areas, and target entry-level role.
Summary.missing: The objective does not distinguish your logistics, inventory, scheduling, or reporting background from broad entry-level motivation.
Summary.working: It identifies operations management as the intended direction and establishes that you are a recent business graduate.

Work Experience.fix: Rewrite the recent operations bullets with verified workload, process details, and results; remove repeated duty phrasing.
Work Experience.missing: The section lacks measurable scale, outcomes, named systems, and clear boundaries around what you personally handled.
Work Experience.working: The sequence shows increasing relevance from Sales Associate to Team Coordinator, Operations Intern, and Operations Assistant.

strengths: The progression from Team Coordinator to Operations Assistant gives the resume a sensible entry-level operations direction.
Greenfield Logistics, MetroRetail Inc., and the Campus Events Office cover records, reporting, inventory, schedules, and event logistics.
The Campus Events Office role includes managing volunteer schedules and recording expenses, which are concrete responsibilities worth retaining.
report.summary: Your recent path points toward entry-level operations work, moving from campus event coordination into retail operations and then Greenfield Logistics. The useful thread is recurring coordination of records, reports, schedules, inventory, and departments. The page does not yet show the scale or result of that work, so it supports coordinator or assistant roles more readily than operations management roles. The practical question is what you personally handled and improved, because that determines whether employers see hands-on readiness or general exposure.
